environment.execution: rootful Docker with pinned distinct physical CPUs

diagnostic_observations.full_stream: All bounded policies reduced the median receipt mean by 14.85-16.84 ms in this run; the adaptive policy reduced median child CPU by 80 ms.
diagnostic_observations.unique_edge: Fixed policies reduced median child CPU by 70-110 ms; receipt-mean deltas were mixed and not a supported latency win.

decision: Retain CONTINUOUS as the production default. Every paired workload interval includes zero, so no bounded policy has a supported performance win. The syscall-dense workload observed only 5-11 idle polls per profiled fork under bounded policies; it does not measure long-idle CPU behavior. Bounded policies remain an explicit integration option, not a default optimization.
next_required_measurement: Run a five-fork sparse-burst workload with controlled idle gaps, reporting paired workload, CPU, receipt-age, parking, loss, and attribution-completeness intervals before considering a production default change.
